hints: Group terms in $z$ to obtain $(1 + 3\mathrm{i})z = 9 + 7\mathrm{i}$, then multiply by conjugate $1 - 3\mathrm{i}$ to find $x + y\mathrm{i}$.
walkthrough:
Expand both sides, remembering $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$5z - 15\mathrm{i} = (2 - 9\mathrm{i})z + (2 - 9\mathrm{i})(3\mathrm{i})$$
Compute the constant product:
$$(2 - 9\mathrm{i})(3\mathrm{i}) = 6\mathrm{i} - 27\mathrm{i}^2 = 6\mathrm{i} - 27(-1) = 27 + 6\mathrm{i}$$
So:
$$5z - 15\mathrm{i} = (2 - 9\mathrm{i})z + 27 + 6\mathrm{i}$$

Collect terms in $z$ on the left-hand side and constants on the right-hand side:
$$5z - (2 - 9\mathrm{i})z = 27 + 6\mathrm{i} + 15\mathrm{i}$$
$$(5 - 2 + 9\mathrm{i})z = 27 + 21\mathrm{i}$$
$$(3 + 9\mathrm{i})z = 27 + 21\mathrm{i}$$

Divide both sides by $3$ to simplify coefficients:
$$(1 + 3\mathrm{i})z = 9 + 7\mathrm{i}$$

Isolate $z$ and multiply numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate $1 - 3\mathrm{i}$:
$$z = \dfrac{9 + 7\mathrm{i}}{1 + 3\mathrm{i}} = \dfrac{(9 + 7\mathrm{i})(1 - 3\mathrm{i})}{(1 + 3\mathrm{i})(1 - 3\mathrm{i})}$$
